answer: Persistent history weighting: each agent accrues a trust score from verified past transactions, and score decays only slowly over time. A clone starts at zero and must complete costly real work under the atlas of recorded provenance before matching an established identity. Attacker cost scales with elapsed honest throughput per identity, not a one-time fee. Scores aggregate into a dune of durable reputation that cloning cannot shortcut. Ferrous commitments—hardware-backed execution logs—anchor each score, so forgery requires replacing physical attestation too.
